findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

The sealant between the counter and the wall to the right of the dish machine was observed heavily soiled in black residue. The PIC is new to the kitchen and was unaware of the ongoing violations. The PIC stated that a maintenance request will be submitted today for the sealant to be replaced. Ensure this sealant is monitored and replaced as needed, as moisture from the dish machine will cause it to degrade over time.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at time of inspection. The PIC stated that the food manager will arrive later in the day. Ensure there is a CFPM present during all times of food preparation and service.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employee improperly hand wash before donning new gloves. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are using hand soap to wash and washing for a minimum of 20 seconds every time they need to don new gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a tray of pulled pork dated 1/12 in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed that the pork was held beyond its 7-day date mark. The tray was discarded. Ensure staff are monitoring food in the walk-in cooler and discarding at the end of day 7.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employee improperly hand wash before donning new gloves. The employee quickly rinsed their hands with water but failed to use soap. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are using hand soap to wash and washing for a minimum of 20 seconds.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution available during food preparation. Staff were slicing tomatoes and cooking bacon with no available sanitizer. A bucket was prepared during the inspection, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are available at all times of food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop stored in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to the strainer portion of the bucket. Advised cook staff to dump mop water immediately after mopping, and to store mop either hanging or placed in strainer to allow for proper drip-drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be present within facility. PIC was unable to provide proof of food handler’s certificates for all employees. Ensure all food handling employees have at least a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed 2 containers of cooked beef and I ziploc bag of cooked chicken in Walk In Cooler with no date mark. Items were discarded during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed containers used to store clean cookware and dish ware to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize containers. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop head to be stored head down on floor of mop sink. Store wet mop head in a fashion that promotes drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed not all food employees of facility to have at least a food handler certification. All food employees at facility must have at least a food handler certification. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
